# odd-flow Claude Code and Codex plugin for Organic Driven Development (ODD): Engram memory discipline and Orca role workers with per-role agent, model and effort profiles. Each profile runs the orchestrator in one of two peer modes: `organic` (inline by default, delegation for a named reason) or `full-delegation` (bounded writers make workspace changes, in Git or not, except for the [parent's closed write list](skills/odd-flow/references/mode-full-delegation.md#who-writes)). In both modes, the parent writes a user-named file outside the workspace only after the user confirms the exact diff. Outside an Orca terminal, delegated roles run as subagents; in organic mode, inline when no subagent can run. ## Contents | Path | Purpose | |---|---| | `skills/odd-flow/` | The `odd-flow` skill (progressive disclosure: `SKILL.md` plus references and assets) | | `hooks/hooks.json` | Claude Code hooks: `SessionStart` on startup, resume, clear and compact; `UserPromptSubmit` and `PreToolUse` | | `hooks/codex-hooks.json` | Codex hooks: `SessionStart` on startup, resume, clear and compact; `UserPromptSubmit`; `PreToolUse` for `apply_patch`, `spawn_agent` and `Bash` | | `scripts/session-start.py` | Injects the core block of the session's mode (`assets/core-block.md` or `assets/core-block-full-delegation.md`) and the active profile into the session | | `scripts/prompt-submit.py` | Records a per-session parent or worker marker from the first prompt. On each prompt, restates full delegation to the coordinator or gives the worker role context. Adds no context in organic mode. | | `scripts/pre-tool-use.py` | Checks edit surface declarations for supported writer launches in both modes; guards the parent's direct Claude Code edits and direct Codex `apply_patch` calls in full delegation | | `.claude-plugin/` | Claude Code plugin manifest and marketplace | | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` | Codex plugin manifest pointing to the shared skill and Codex hooks | | `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | Codex marketplace | In full delegation, the [parent edit guard](skills/odd-flow/references/mode-full-delegation.md#parent-edit-guard) checks Claude Code `Edit`, `Write` and `NotebookEdit` calls and Codex direct local `apply_patch` calls. It does not guard `Bash` writes. If Orca changes its preamble and no recognized `# Role:` header starts the prompt, a Claude worker is treated as the parent. The guard covers `Edit`, `Write` and `NotebookEdit` with Code Mode on or off. Code Mode REPL `write()` and `edit()` reach the hook as `Write` and `Edit`. ## Install (Claude Code) ```sh claude plugin marketplace add alvag/odd-flow claude plugin install odd-flow@odd-flow ``` For development, run `claude plugin marketplace add "$PWD"` from the checkout instead, or try it without installing with `claude --plugin-dir "$PWD"`. Verified on 2026-11-24 at `bc59916` with a scratch home and Claude config: marketplace add cloned over SSH. With SSH disabled, it printed “SSH clone failed, retrying with HTTPS” and succeeded. Installation reported `0.1.0`; `diff -rq --exclude=.git` against an extracted `git archive HEAD` found only Claude's `.in_use` marker. The skill is invoked as `/odd-flow:odd-flow`. A plain `/odd-flow` was not expanded as a skill call in a headless session (2026-11-23) and reached the model only as text; interactive sessions are unchecked. Profile commands: `/odd-flow:odd-flow --profile

` (this session), `--profile-default

`, `--profiles` (list, then pick one for the session or as default), `--create-profile

` (guided, from the agents and models Orca and Codex report), `--mode ` (this session) and `--profile-mode

` (saved in the profile, after you confirm the diff). ## Install (Codex) With Codex CLI 0.171.0 and Python 3 available: ```sh codex plugin marketplace add alvag/odd-flow --ref main codex plugin add odd-flow@odd-flow ``` For development, run `codex plugin marketplace add "$PWD"` from the checkout instead. Codex installs a copy in its plugin cache (`~/.codex/plugins/cache/odd-flow/odd-flow/`). Reinstall the plugin after changing the checkout; edits do not reach the cached copy. Review the odd-flow hooks in Codex with `/hooks` and trust them if you want to enable them. Verified on 2026-11-24 at `bc59916` with a scratch home and `CODEX_HOME`: the commands above installed `0.1.0`; `diff -rq --exclude=.git` against an extracted `git archive HEAD` found no differences. On 2026-11-23, running `codex plugin add odd-flow@odd-flow` at the same version refreshed the `0.1.0` cache. A `diff -rq --exclude=.git` against the checkout found seven differing files and a missing `tests/codex-runtime-check.sh` before reinstalling, and no differences afterward. The cache copy also includes untracked files such as `odd/tasks/codex-packaging.md`. With Codex CLI 0.171.0, SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit completed in each live `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` run. Asked to list the short replies under “Authorized work continuity” without using tools, the parent returned “yes”, “go ahead”, and “eso mismo”, which only the core block lists. A `# Role: write` worker wrote `hello.txt` with a single shell command, made no Orca or subagent attempt, answered `ROLE`, and had a `worker` marker. Codex uses its own `PreToolUse` manifest. In full delegation, it checks every target of a coordinator's direct local `apply_patch` call. In either mode, it checks the allowed edit surfaces of identifiable writer launches through supported native `spawn_agent` and local Orca forms. It does not enforce writer surfaces after launch or inspect shell write targets. See the [parent edit guard](skills/odd-flow/references/mode-full-delegation.md#parent-edit-guard) and [writer surface checks](skills/odd-flow/references/delegation.md#allowed-edit-surfaces). ## Install (Antigravity) Clone the GitHub repository first: `agy plugin install` needs a local directory for this plugin. ```sh git clone https://github.com/alvag/odd-flow agy plugin install ./odd-flow ``` For development, run `agy plugin install "$PWD"` from the checkout instead. Reinstall after changing the checkout, and review the plugin's hook in Antigravity before relying on it. The package is a native Antigravity CLI plugin for `agy` 1.5.16 (https://antigravity.google/docs/build-plugins). `.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json` selects the shared `skills/odd-flow` skill, and the root `hooks.json` registers a flat `SessionStart` handler (`python3 -I ./scripts/session-start.py --runtime antigravity`), a flat `PreInvocation` handler (`scripts/prompt-submit.py --runtime antigravity`: worker marking and full-delegation reinjection on the first invocation of each turn, `invocationNum == 0`; the counter is 0-indexed in `agy` 1.5.16 and defaults to `0` when omitted) and a grouped `PreToolUse` handler (`scripts/pre-tool-use.py --runtime antigravity`: parent edit guard for the file-edit tools and writer launch admission for `run_command` and `invoke_subagent`). The hook reads the payload's `conversationId`, uses it as `ANTIGRAVITY_CONVERSATION_ID` for profile resolution (an inherited Claude or Codex id never overrides it), and returns the core block and active profile as an `injectSteps` system message. Validate a checkout without installing it, with a scratch home: ```sh scratch=$(mktemp -d) mkdir -p "$scratch/home" "$scratch/config" "$scratch/data" HOME="$scratch/home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$scratch/config" XDG_DATA_HOME="$scratch/data" agy plugin validate --json "$PWD" ``` The expected result is one skill, one hook, no errors, and one warning: `hooks/hooks.json` is never loaded because Antigravity reads plugin hooks only from the root `hooks.json`. That file belongs to Claude Code. A missing logo is informational. Verified on 2026-11-24 at `bc59916`: `agy plugin validate --json` on a fresh HTTPS clone reported one skill, one hook, the `hooks/hooks.json` warning, and the missing-logo note. - Validation: `agy plugin validate`, above. - Hook fixtures: `tests/antigravity-plugin-check.sh`, which runs the hook script directly and needs no `agy` binary. - Installed-session smoke test: see the live verification below. Verified live on 2026-11-24 in the installed plugin with `agy` 1.5.16 inside Orca (`main` `4c3d8a2`): `PreInvocation` fired, and `PreToolUse` denied `write_file` (argument `Path`; the file was not created), `invoke_subagent` (argument `Prompt`; missing `## Allowed edit surfaces`) and `run_command` (argument `CommandLine`; unparseable Orca launch). `invocationNum` is 0-indexed: `0` on the first model call of a turn and `1` on the second, after tool calls. Also verified live on 2026-11-24 (installed odd-flow 0.2.0 matching `main` `edcf3e0`, `agy` 1.5.16 in Orca, default `claude-gpt` full delegation): the guard denied the coordinator's `edit_file` and left the workspace file unchanged. An external, non-temp `write_file` returned `force_ask` and showed a Create file confirmation; declining left the file absent. In a new session, `edit_file` succeeded after a first prompt starting with `# Role: write` in a plain Orca terminal. Not validated live or promised: `write_to_file`, `replace_file_content` and `multi_replace_file_content`, mode reinjection mid-session, the profile identity of an interactive `agy` session, and Orca worker enforcement for Antigravity, including the Orca dispatch preamble marker. ## Updating Claude Code enables auto-update per marketplace. It defaults to on for official marketplaces and off for third-party GitHub marketplaces like `alvag/odd-flow`. To enable it, run `/plugin`, open **Marketplaces**, select **odd-flow**, and turn on auto-update. See [Install and manage plugins](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/install.md). After the first message in an interactive session, Claude Code waits a random delay of up to ten minutes, then refreshes the marketplace and updates installed plugins on disk. Run `/reload-plugins` to apply the update now, or let the next launch load it. Setting `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, `DISABLE_UPDATES=1`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` disables this pass unless `FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS=1` is also set. See the [Plugin loading reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md). Codex and Antigravity do not auto-update; use the manual commands below. Claude Code can also update manually. - Claude Code: run `claude plugin marketplace update odd-flow`, then `claude plugin update odd-flow@odd-flow` and restart Claude Code. - Codex: run `codex plugin marketplace upgrade odd-flow`, then `codex plugin add odd-flow@odd-flow`. - Antigravity: from the parent directory of the clone, run `git -C ./odd-flow pull`, then `agy plugin install ./odd-flow`. Claude Code detects updates by reading `version` from `plugin.json` first, then from the marketplace entry if the manifest omits it. odd-flow pins its version, so Claude Code users won't receive a push without a version bump, even with auto-update enabled. For every change published to `main` that users should receive, bump `version` to the same value in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, the `odd-flow` entry in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, and `.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json`. Add an entry for the new version to [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and check with `bash tests/version-check.sh`. ## Profiles File at `~/.config/odd-flow/profiles.json`, edited by hand or through the profile commands (override with `ODD_FLOW_HOME`). See `skills/odd-flow/references/profiles.md` and `skills/odd-flow/assets/profiles.example.json`. ## Other runtimes For an agent without the plugin, `skills/odd-flow/scripts/init.py` can write the core block into the global instructions file (see `skills/odd-flow/references/init.md`). To validate a writer spec without a supported launch hook, run `python3 -I skills/odd-flow/scripts/surface.py check `. ## Checks - Run all test suites with `bash tests/run.sh`. - `claude plugin validate .` - `echo '{"source":"startup"}' | python3 -I scripts/session-start.py`
